surprises: The verification's suggested_text for inspect.md:64 included the sentence 'the command resolves the repository itself and takes no repository-root argument'. The second half is true, the first half is false: the Go runtime defaults RepositoryRoot to os.Getwd() (command_runtime.go:103-107), and from a subdirectory `associate` exits 2 silently with do-work/ present. That draft was not used. It is a fifth false draft of the same compression shape the request warns about.

The current-directory dependence is a property of the launcher shared by both callers: scripts/protected-inventory.sh puts "$@" after the command token, so a --repo-root global flag cannot reach the runtime through it, and neither commit.md nor inspect.md can pass a root. A mechanical fix would live in the launcher (one place, both callers), not in per-action prose; that is a code change outside this REQ's write set and is worth a REQ like REQ-601. board.md:84 already uses a `(cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)" && <skill-root>/...)` subshell prefix for a launcher call, so a per-block form exists if the maintainer prefers it over the launcher change.

So the two exit-2 causes that inspect.md:117 folds together are distinguishable by output: a usage error (unknown option, quarantine not started, outside a repository) prints a `finding HELPER-USAGE [error]: ...` block on stdout, while the missing-do-work skip prints nothing. Line 117 could key the skip on 'exit 2 with no output' and treat a printed HELPER-USAGE finding as a broken invocation to report — the exact distinction that would have caught this defect. Left for builder 3, who owns line 117.

sentences.old_phrase: Both own the clock, so no caller derives a timestamp with `date` and no caller invents a second duration format.
sentences.new_text: Neither accepts a duration — elapsed seconds are always derived by the command — so no caller invents a second duration format. `run-timed-command` owns both ends of its interval. `record-timing-event` stamps the end itself and, given no start, chains the start to the previous event's end (or to its own end on an empty stream); `--started-at <RFC3339>` pins the start to an instant the caller already held, which is how `actions/work.md` records a delegated builder wait, and the instant it holds comes from the Timestamp rule in `actions/work-reference.md`, whose POSIX floor is `date -u`.

sentences.old_phrase: The canonical command copies and verifies that source into a private file adjacent to the canonical target, once per output.

Fresh case each time: .stage holds PAYLOAD, occupied_file holds OLD, occupied_dir is an empty directory. (1) rename over a regular file: rename(2) via python os.rename returned 0 and occupied_file now reads PAYLOAD; Go os.Rename -> nil, Root.Rename -> nil, file replaced; shell `mv .stage occupied_file` -> exit 0, replaced. (2) rename over a directory: rename(2) -> errno 21 EISDIR, nothing written; Go os.Rename -> 'rename ...: file exists' (Go's own pre-check maps it to EEXIST), Root.Rename -> 'renameat .stage occupied_dir: is a directory'; directory left with 0 entries in every case; shell `mv .stage occupied_dir` -> exit 0 and .stage moved INSIDE occupied_dir. (3) link over a regular file: link(2) via os.link -> errno 17 EEXIST; Go os.Link and Root.Link -> 'file exists'; shell `ln .stage occupied_file` -> exit 1 'failed to create hard link: File exists'. (4) link over a directory: link(2) -> EEXIST; Go os.Link -> 'file exists', Root.Link -> 'linkat .stage occupied_dir: file exists', directory 0 entries; shell `ln .stage occupied_dir` -> exit 0 and a hard link named .stage created INSIDE occupied_dir. Derived sentences: mv and ln nest into an occupying directory and exit 0; link(2) refuses every existing destination; rename(2) refuses a directory and silently replaces a regular file. Because os.Rename reports 'file exists' while rename(2)/Root.Rename report EISDIR, the guide does not name an errno for the shipped helpers' directory refusal.
